critique.good: The paired name columns have equal visual weight, prices align on one line, and all headers remain intact. The short second row is easy to scan.
critique.problems: The first and third descriptions occupy three lines, making those rows tall and leaving substantial empty space beneath the shorter names and prices.
critique.cause: The 180px description column has only 159px for text. The 110px and 111px name columns take space that could help the longer descriptions.

critique.good: This is the strongest overall balance: descriptions fit within two lines, prices remain intact, and the similar name-column widths reinforce the Thai–Lao pairing. Rows are compact while still reading as units.
critique.problems: The longest Thai and Lao dish names wrap, making the last row's name area feel noticeably tighter than the description area. The wide description column also leaves unused space in the short middle row.
critique.cause: The 88px and 89px name columns provide only 67px and 68px of text width. The 224px description column receives much of the available space.

critique.good: The wider paired name columns let the longest dish names stay on one line, and prices and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: Descriptions feel cramped and dominate the row heights. Even the short middle description wraps, while the first and last rows have large areas of empty space under their names and prices.
critique.cause: The 148px description column leaves only 127px for text, while the 126px and 127px name columns consume more width than most names need.

critique.good: The Thai and Lao names have balanced weight, prices align on one line, and the description has enough space to keep the rows relatively compact. Headers and words remain intact.
critique.problems: Both names in the last row wrap, making that dish harder to scan across the paired columns. The description also wraps in the first and last rows.
critique.cause: The 94px and 95px name columns provide 73px and 74px of text space, less than the widest names need. The 212px description column cannot hold the longest descriptions on one line.

critique.good: The paired name columns remain balanced, prices stay intact, and the row heights match r1A. The slightly wider name columns give the names more breathing room.
critique.problems: The last-row names still wrap, so the extra width does not visibly resolve the main limitation of r1A. The narrower description column also leaves less room for descriptions.
critique.cause: At 100px and 101px, the name columns still fall short of the 126px and 127px needed for their widest one-line contents. Reducing the description to 200px does not reduce any row height.

critique.good: The wide description column gives the descriptive text a more generous measure, and prices and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: The name columns are cramped: the Lao name in the second dish wraps, and the final Thai name spreads over three lines. This disrupts the paired-name comparison and makes the last two rows taller.
critique.cause: Widths of 84px and 85px leave only 63px and 64px for names. The extra space given to the 232px description column does not compensate for the resulting name wraps.

critique.good: The paired name columns have balanced weight, prices align on one line, and the description has enough room to keep every row to at most two lines. The resulting rows are easy to scan across.
critique.problems: The longest Thai and Lao dish names both wrap, making the last row denser on the left than the others.
critique.cause: The 105px and 106px name columns provide 84px and 85px of text space, less than the longest one-line names require.

critique.good: The wider, similarly sized name columns keep the dish names on one line, and the prices remain easy to compare.
critique.problems: Descriptions become narrow blocks of up to three lines, including a two-line description in the middle row. This produces tall rows and leaves substantial empty space under the names and prices.
critique.cause: The 126px and 127px name columns take space from the description, leaving it only 148px wide, or 127px of text space.

critique.good: The paired names remain visually balanced, prices stay on one line, and the middle row is compact.
critique.problems: The longest names still wrap, while the first and last descriptions each occupy three lines. The small gain in name-column width therefore comes with a substantial increase in row height.
critique.cause: At 110px and 111px, the name columns are still too narrow for the longest names; reducing the description to 180px crosses wrapping thresholds for two descriptions.

understanding.purpose: Present a Thai–Lao menu with prices and descriptions so readers can identify and compare dishes.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the two dish-name columns to find a dish, then read across the row for its price and description.
groups: Columns 1 and 2 pair Thai and Lao names for the same dishes, so they should have similar visual weight and width.
Columns 3 and 4 provide the price and description for each dish.
keep_intact: Prices and their currency should remain on one line for easy comparison.
Individual words in dish names and descriptions should remain intact.
may_wrap: Longer dish names can wrap at natural word boundaries.
Descriptions can wrap across multiple lines; their row height can also accommodate wrapping in the paired dish names.

bad.why: The narrow name columns break several dish names across lines, including a three-line Thai name, while the description column has more width than it needs.
The wide name columns leave the descriptions cramped: every description wraps, two to three lines, making the rows taller and harder to scan.
The description column produces three-line entries with short final lines, disrupting the rhythm of the first and last data rows.
Like r2B, its narrow description column forces excessive wrapping and makes the table unnecessarily tall.

final.rationale: The Thai and Lao dish names play equivalent roles, so r2A gives them nearly equal widths and keeps their wrapping balanced. The price column fits its values on one line, while the description column is wide enough to keep every entry to at most two lines. The resulting rows remain easy to scan across within the viewport.

general: Give columns that play equivalent roles comparable space, adjusted for their content.
Allocate width where it reduces disruptive wrapping, while preserving clear row-by-row comparison.
specific: Here the price values fit in 78px, leaving useful space for the two language columns and descriptions.
The tested width combinations from r1B through r2A retain the same row heights and avoid mid-word splits.

final.tradeoffs: A designer might prefer r1B or r3B for the extra description width; r2A gives the paired dish names slightly more room while retaining the same two-line maximum.
final.uncertain: The ranges describe the tested preferred-quality combinations, not independently adjustable widths: the columns must still total at most 479px. Untested widths between or beyond these points may also work.

A.why: The description has room, but the two food-name columns are cramped: the last Thai name takes three lines, and a Lao name also wraps in the middle row.

B.why: The paired food names have similar widths, prices stay on one line, and the description remains readable. The last row wraps in both name columns and the description.

C.why: The food-name columns are balanced, prices stay intact, and the description has enough room for a steady two-line rhythm where needed.

D.why: The four nearly equal columns give the short prices excessive space and squeeze the descriptions into narrow, fragmented lines. The resulting tall rows are harder to scan.

E.why: The name and description columns have useful space, but every price is split between its number and currency, making the prices harder to compare.

F.why: The two food-name columns are balanced, prices remain on one line, and the description has enough width to avoid excessive wrapping.

reviews.unsure: C and F appear identical at the displayed resolution, so I cannot distinguish a meaningful difference between them. B is also close.

A.why: The two language columns are balanced, prices stay together, and the descriptions remain readable; the longest dish names wrap naturally.

B.why: The narrow language columns break dish names into several short lines, making the paired names harder to scan despite the generous description column.

C.why: The wide price column takes space from the descriptions, which wrap into narrow stacks and make rows unnecessarily tall.

D.why: The paired language columns and intact prices scan well, while the description has enough room for readable lines. Several long names still wrap.

E.why: The paired dish names have room to read, prices remain intact, and descriptions wrap into manageable lines. The columns form a clear, balanced hierarchy.

F.why: The price column splits every amount from its currency, disrupting comparison; its saved space adds little benefit to the descriptions.

reviews.unsure: A and D are very close to E; the relative readability of the Thai and Lao line breaks is difficult to judge at this image size.
